Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings:  34-year-old with 6 weeks of intermittent unilateral (left) hearing reduction, unilateral tinnitus that can improve with external sound (TV/music), and intermittent mild imbalance. No ear pain, discharge, fever. Denies cotton bud use. Prior brief similar episode ~1 year ago.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  - Cerumen impaction causing unilateral conductive hearing loss with tinnitus—common, painless, and requires otoscopy to confirm.
  - Early/probable Ménière disease—unilateral tinnitus with fluctuating hearing issues and episodic imbalance; absence of true spinning vertigo or aural fullness makes this less classic but still possible.
  - Eustachian tube dysfunction/otitis media with effusion—could cause unilateral, fluctuating conductive loss and tinnitus without pain; no URI/allergy history reported.
  - Vestibular schwannoma—less likely given short time course and age, but unilateral hearing loss with tinnitus and imbalance warrants consideration if symptoms persist or progress.
- Working diagnosis:  Unilateral hearing loss with tinnitus—etiology unclear. Plan to first exclude external ear canal obstruction (e.g., cerumen) via otoscopy.
- Management priorities:  Arrange face-to-face ear examination to assess for wax or other physical obstruction; provide tinnitus education; safety-net advice.

Management Plan

- Actions and recommendations provided:
  - Face-to-face clinic appointment to examine ears (otoscopy) within 4–5 days; not an emergency.
  - Educational resource: Link to tinnitus information provided; patient asked to review before in-person visit.
  - Safety net: Contact support team to schedule; if any worsening or new issues before the visit, book another appointment or seek care.
- Follow-up: In-person GP review in 4–5 days to check ears and guide next steps based on findings.
- Reflective reasoning (from DDx, aligned with plan): Initial focus on excluding cerumen impaction or other obstructive causes; if otoscopy is normal and symptoms persist, further evaluation for inner ear or retrocochlear causes may be considered (context only; not ordered during this visit).

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Face-to-face ear exam booked in 4–5 days; other preventive follow-ups not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Cerumen impaction (Moderate): Painless unilateral hearing reduction with tinnitus over weeks; otoscopy needed to confirm; aligns with clinician’s plan to exclude wax first.
- Early/probable Ménière disease (Moderate): Unilateral tinnitus with fluctuating hearing and episodic imbalance; lack of true vertigo reduces classic fit but remains plausible.
- Eustachian tube dysfunction/otitis media with effusion (Low-Moderate): Unilateral, fluctuating conductive loss and tinnitus without pain or fever; no URI/allergy history reported.
